html:
The Chukchansi are a Foothill Yokuts people of the Sierra Nevada foothills in central California, around today's Coarsegold and Oakhurst, north of Fresno. They lived in villages along the creeks between the San Joaquin and Fresno rivers, eating acorns, seeds, fish and game. Their northern neighbours were the Southern Sierra Miwok.

The Gold Rush brought miners into their hills, and in the Mariposa War of 1850 and 1851 state militia fought the local peoples and forced them onto reservations. Today the Chukchansi are part of the Picayune Rancheria. The tribe has funded work to record and teach the Chukchansi language, one of the few Yokuts languages still spoken.
